what: The Fp32Mode enum doc says Lossless is "rarely useful — you almost never want Lossless" and lists three conditions that all assume the tiled output is consumed by SFPU/FPU inside the SAME kernel. For a STANDALONE tilize op whose output is a user-visible tensor with a bit-identity oracle, Lossless is MANDATORY (Fast truncates fp32->tf32 into the stored result, so fp32->fp32 stops being bit-exact and the golden comp_equal gate fails). The doc as written steers an agent to Fast and a silent precision regression; I had to re-derive the exception from the oracle.
suggest: Add one bullet to the Fp32Mode enum comment: "Exception — when the tiled output IS the op result (a standalone tilize/layout-conversion op with a value-preserving contract), Lossless is required for fp32 input: Fast truncates fp32->tf32 in the stored tensor. The rely-on-Fast argument only holds when a same-kernel FPU consumer would re-truncate anyway."

ref: incremental-verifier agent prompt: § Implementation skill inventory + § Building op_requirements.md
what: The queue-building guidance assumes SUPPORTED is a proper subset of TARGET. This op arrived with SUPPORTED == TARGET on every axis (perf-focused run, Phase 0 landed the whole matrix), so xfail_expected was 0 ENTRIES and every grouping rule (bundle dtypes, bundle layouts, TARGET-SUPPORTED per axis) was inapplicable. The only applicable guidance is one clause of the hard rule (concrete perf lever + measured gap) plus the single Mode-D exception, and the skill-inventory table contains NO perf skill even though the hard rule mandates a /perf-measure or /perf-ceiling-dm pointer for those entries — so "attach a pointer if it matches a skill in the inventory above" and "must carry a /perf-measure pointer" contradict each other. A future verifier could plausibly ship an empty queue or vague perf notes.
suggest: (1) Add /perf-measure and /perf-ceiling-dm rows to the skill-inventory table with their scopes. (2) Add a short "perf-only queue" playbook: when TARGET-SUPPORTED is empty, refinements are levers with a measured off-ceiling gap read off the implementer changelog perf table, each naming lever + shape + achieved ratio, ordered by dependency, with exactly one run-closing Mode-D audit last.

ref: incremental-verifier agent prompt: § Registry Conformance ("Confirm the four declarations")
what: The conformance checklist enumerates exactly four declarations (INPUT_TAGGERS, SUPPORTED, EXCLUSIONS, validate) and instructs deleting any extra registry-looking symbol (INVALID). The op file also declares PROPERTIES, which IS legitimate (optional block 3b in eval/op_template.py, consumed by eval/dump_op_metadata.py and eval/features_table.py) — but the verifier prompt never mentions it, so the "delete non-template symbols" instinct points at a load-bearing declaration. I had to grep eval/ to confirm it was not cruft.
suggest: Mention PROPERTIES in the Registry Conformance checklist as an optional fifth declaration: what it is for (non-axis capability facts feeding the Features tab), and that the verifier should check the value/source tags are honest ("verified" only when automated evidence exists) rather than delete it.
